articles.title: The Elder Scrolls Doesn't Have a New Vegas-Like Spinoff Because Todd Howard Is 'Very Protective' of the Franchise, Former Dev Claims
articles.summary: The Elder Scrolls never got a Fallout: New Vegas -like spinoff because Todd Howard is "very protective" of the IP, according to former Bethesda developer Kurt Kuhlmann.
body: Kuhlmann, who served as lead designer and senior designer at the Microsoft studio for 20 years before leaving in 2023, shared details on his experience working on the legendary fantasy RPG franchise during an interview with FRVR. Fans have spent decades wondering why The Elder Scrolls never got the same spinoff treatment as Fallout has, but he said there's a pretty specific reason why that's the case.

"The whole New Vegas thing did create this, at least the perception of this, 'Who makes a better Fallout game? Oh, they should just give it to Obsidian’," Kuhlmann said. "There are the Obsidian, the New Vegas people, that think obviously New Vegas is way better, Obsidian is way better at making those games, and why don’t they just get Fallout altogether?"
Kuhlmann isn't sure "that Todd wanted to create that situation again for The Elder Scrolls." He added, "Todd, from my time there, he is very protective of it."
points: The Elder Scrolls never got a Fallout: New Vegas -like spinoff because Todd Howard is "very protective" of the IP, according to former Bethesda developer Kurt Kuhlmann.

articles.title: Backrooms Director Kane Parsons Wants a Limited Series to Pull Off Horror Franchise's 'Main Ending'
articles.summary: Backrooms director Kane Parsons says he’s always had a “main ending” in mind for his liminal space story, which he says would be best served as a limited series. Parsons, while not the original creator of the viral 4Chan greentext post responsible for kicking off the Backrooms craze, is arguably…
body: Ever since he first shared his videos — which were almost entirely created in the 3D software Blender — he’s had an idea about how he wants his Backrooms saga to end, though it likely won’t be in theaters.
Speaking to Deadline, Parsons said there’s “always been a plan” for its ending, though it’s been challenging to “find the proper way to package that.”

“I never stop making things,” he told the outlet. “There’s a few things that I would love to talk about when I can soon. I’ve said since the very beginning that the dream scenario would be a limited series for Backrooms to get to the main ending.
“I can’t say anything, but there’s been a very set arc to the whole thing from the beginning, and I just feel absurdly excited at the idea of actually being able to follow through on all of it.”

articles.title: Activision Keeps Saying All The Right Things About Modern Warfare 4
articles.summary: Activision has made a key announcement about how Double XP tokens work in the upcoming Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and it sounds like good news. Beginning with MW4, 2XP tokens will only count down when you're actually in a match.
body: If you're anything like me, sometimes you have to get up to let your dog out. Or you want to get up to grab some food or a drink. Or, you might sit in the game's menus when nature calls. Now, you can do those things and still get the full amount of 2XP without your bonus going to waste.

Beyond this, several key developers at Infinity Ward discussed a range of hot topics about MW4 in a newly published "The Road to Launch" video. Check it out below to hear what the team had to say about time-to-kill values, spawning algorithms, and UI issues following the game's multiple rounds of beta testing.

This is just the latest positive-sounding update for MW4, following the previous confirmation that players will be able to toggle off skins they don't want to see in Warzone --though the toggle is not supported for MW4 itself yet.

Modern Warfare 4 launches on October 23 for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC. The game marks the first Call of Duty release on a Nintendo platform since 2013's Call of Duty: Ghosts. It's also the first game since Ghosts to skip PS4 and Xbox One.

articles.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Is Reportedly Already Planning a Re-Release With New Footage
articles.summary: Deadline has reported that Sony is preparing a new cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which will be released into theaters in the future. There's currently no word on when this re-release will drop, but the window for it to happen this year is rapidly shrinking as the holiday season approaches.
body: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is reportedly already planning a re-release, which will feature new footage.

This isn't the first time Sony has done this for the webhead. In 2022, the company re-released Spider-Man: No Way Home with additional footage, including extended scenes featuring all three Spider-Men. Admittedly, it wasn't anything to write home about, and it was arguably a worse movie due to how these extra scenes disrupted its overall pacing. It added about 10 extra minutes to the original film, so it's possible something similar will happen here with Brand New Day.

Similarly, Avengers: Endgame is cleaning up at the box office seven years after its release thanks to a new re-release, which adds newly-shot footage that connects it to Avengers: Doomsday. All of these re-releases seem to be done with at least a partial goal of boosting the film's box office numbers; Brand New Day is currently the number one film at the domestic box office, and third globally. Avengers: Endgame's re-release is allowing it to quickly close the gap between it and the number one film, Avatar.

articles.title: WoW: Forever’s Beta Just Keeps Getting Bigger
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever's beta is in full swing, and if its popularity is any indication of how the full launch might go, it's going to be big, as Blizzard has had to increase the beta's population cap multiple times.
body: Forever was Blizzard's big finale during its BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony, a modified version of WoW Classic that keeps the old-school MMORPG's gameplay and world but brings plenty of new changes and content as well. It's something WoW Classic players have asked for years, and Blizzard is now finally ready to deliver.

The beta kicked off September 17 with an initial level cap of 20 and will run through October 21, with Forever's full launch slated for November 4. It's important to note that it's not an open beta that anyone can join. Players need to purchase the $60 Skyborne Epic Pack (which unlocks the new playable Skyborne race in Forever) to gain access.

Despite a $60 barrier to entry, everything points towards the beta being huge. From the get go, the beta ran into problems due to sheer popularity, with WoW: Forever senior game producer Tom Ellis (who has since deleted their X account ) posting a technical breakdown that boiled many of the beta's initial issues down to the game's beta environment simply not being accustomed to such high demand.

articles.title: For The First Time Ever, Sony Skips CES, Which Was Home To One Of PlayStation’s Silliest Announcements
articles.summary: Sony has attended every edition of the Consumer Electronics Show (CES) since it debuted in 1967, but that's ending for the upcoming show in January 2027. This means there won't be any PlayStation news, at least not directly from Sony.
body: The company confirmed to Bloomberg that it's pulling out of the show this year following a strategic evaluation of its approach to "events and communications based on the needs and priorities of our diverse business."
The company went on to say that today it's putting more focus on "entertainment," including games, anime, films, and music. CES, on the other hand, is primarily a technology show.

Sony's showing at CES historically includes a keynote address, featuring executives and creative leaders from the company discussing upcoming technologies and products. Sony never made the most momentous PlayStation announcements at its CES events over the years, but it was an event that fans could expect some news, at least.

For example, in 2020, then-PlayStation boss Jim Ryan revealed the PS5 logo at CES. At the time, people were clamoring for any morsel of news about the console, and fans roasted Sony for revealing only the logo. You can re-live the moment where everyone learned that the logo would be the most predictable logo ever in the video below. The juicier details like the release date, price, and technical specifics were saved for later events dedicated to the system.

articles.title: GTA 6’s $400 Collector’s Edition Is the Latest Example of a Horrible Trend
articles.summary: Spendy deluxe editions are nothing new in the world of video games. For many years now, players have had the option to pay a bit more than retail price — often between $20 and $50 extra — for a bundle of extra goodies to enhance a new game they're looking forward to playing.
body: Last week, Rockstar revealed its Goodtime State – Vice City Collection collectors box for GTA 6, a $400 assortment of branded merch that does not include a copy of the game. It's the latest example of how the industry has pivoted to pursuing high-spending players instead of trying to reach a wider audience.

Back when Sony announced plans to stop producing physical games industry analyst Mat Piscatella pointed out the writing on the wall. "In a world where consoles potentially cost $1k+ the focus shifts from trying to attract the mass market to targeting only the most affluent with the least price sensitivity and highest preference for convenience," he wrote in a July 3 post on Bluesky. If you zoom out a bit, you can see that same strategy at play when it comes to collector's editions, too.

articles.title: Diablo 4 Season 15 Is Filled To The Brim With Big Secrets, And They Just Keep Coming
articles.summary: Diablo 4 Season 15 is stuffed full of secrets years in the making, and despite the season having launched two weeks ago, players keep discovering new ones. Season 15, Hell's Legacy, is a major nostalgia trip for Diablo fans.
body: But those references to previous games go far beyond a handful of dungeons and bosses. It also added a full Horadric Cube's worth of secrets. Some stem from older games in the franchise, while others are a continuation of ones added in Diablo 4 that players have worked towards uncovering for years.

After years of searching, Blizzard finally gave players the culmination of its secret cow-level hunt, as players who have gone through the laborious task of reaching the cow level and battling the cow king can now go even one step further to take on Moophisto, the Divine Bovine. In that same vein, players can also finally catch Mefishto, a secret fishing boss Blizzard went as far as to tease with a bizarre infomercial back when the game's Lord of Hatred expansion launched. Players were also quick to discover all kinds of new runewords and items from previous Diablo games, like the highly coveted Enigma that converts each class' evade into a teleport.

articles.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Getting Official New Version, Report Says
articles.summary: As Marvel Studios' recent release of Avengers Endgame: Encore proves, blockbuster movies can still dominate the box office, even after a multibillion dollar run. Sony is reportedly planning a rerelease of Spider-Man: Brand New Day to bring web-head-heads back to movie theaters — and like Endgame…
body: According to Deadline, the new footage will include at least one cut cameo from Spider-Man: Brand New Day that connects to the larger Marvel Cinematic Universe.

Deadline reports that Sony's planned theatrical rerelease of Spider-Man: Brand New Day will feature extra footage that includes an appearance from Rosario Dawson's character Claire Temple, aka Night Nurse. Dawson played Temple in multiple Netflix Marvel shows: Daredevil, Jessica Jones, Luke Cage, Iron Fist, and The Defenders. The Night Nurse had her own Marvel comic series in the early '70s, in which she tended to the medical needs of New York City's vigilante crime fighters (though that version of the character was named Linda Carter).

Dawson has said in interviews that she filmed a scene that was cut from the theatrical release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Deadline's report implies Sony has more than just a Claire Temple cameo in its pocket, saying there will be "more surprises in the extra footage."

articles.summary: Every service job has that one customer that really has it coming to them. Dressmaker is the rare game that offers you a hilarious opportunity for catharsis, should you be so inclined. On its surface, this is a cozy little sewing sim: You pick fabric, cut a pattern, and stitch buttons on by hand.
body: In the game, you start as a small-town seamstress with a single sewing machine and a waitlist of townsfolk, each one arriving with a specific request: A fabric preference, a color swatch, a trim style. Match all three, deliver on time, and your reputation climbs. The game plays at first like the gentlest possible business sim. That is, of course, before you start reading customer request cards less like checklists and more like dares.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

articles.title: Double Fine's releasing its next game, Thank You Bus Driver, just months after splitting from Xbox
articles.summary: Double Fine's wasted no time at all as an independent game studio (again) after splitting from former owner Xbox earlier this summer. The storied developer is releasing its whacky driving sim, Thank You Bus Driver, in roughly two weeks time.
body: Announced mere weeks ago, Double Fine's first post-Xbox release is a black-and-white "chaotic bus driving game where you take on the role of a town's bus driver just trying to get through the day with minimal rule breaking and maximum gratitude." And, as the studio announced this weekend, it's coming to various PC storefronts on 14 October.
You can find Thank You Bus Driver on Steam, GOG and Itch.io.

Thank You Bus Driver asks you to take passengers to their destinations within a time limit, but the comedy simulation game has an unexpected dash of Paper, Please as well. As the day goes on, you'll need to enforce various rules by turning around and slapping passengers across the face with your freakishly long arms - in case you were wondering where the signature Double Fine twist was hiding.

Of course, this also marks Double Fine's first game since regaining its independence. Xbox's ongoing corporate restructure has seen the console maker spin off five first-party studios, including Double Fine, with plans to lay off around 3,200 staff by next summer. The Psychonauts and Brutal Legend studio laid off a quarter of its own workforce as a result.

articles.title: "What if London existed in the Grand Theft Auto universe?" One fan has answered with a GTA-style map of the city
articles.summary: What if Rockstar created a GTA game set in London?" Anyone sitting in the venn diagram centre of GTA fan and cartography sicko might be happy to learn that YouTuber CityEd has answered both of those questions with a GTA-style map.
body: "I've created a GTA-ised map of London imagining how the map would look, and re-invented place names in a classic GTA style," CityEd wrote on their Patreon, where you can also find a PDF copy of their map. "For instance, Kings Cross becomes 'Dukes Cross', Angel becomes 'Saint'', and the whole city becomes 'Trafalgar'."

CityEd's thought experiment aimed to carry Rockstar Games ' naming conventions across the pond - that includes the developer's signature satire, "exaggerated landmarks and GTA-style cartography" - using the studio's past games as a reference point.

"While the cities and places they base their maps on exist in real life, they have this fun convention for creating fictional place names where they find something historically or culturally associated with the place, exaggerate it, and use that instead," they explained.

As they also noted, Rockstar's last trip to the English capital wasn't much help at all. 1999's GTA: London mission pack didn't bother renaming the city in fun ways, so CityEd's version had to start from scratch.
points: What if Rockstar created a GTA game set in London?

articles.title: Former Elder Scrolls writer Kurt Kuhlmann is '100% convinced' a load-bearing bit of series lore was inspired by a typo
articles.summary: Speaking on the FRVR Podcast last week, former Bethesda writer and designer Kurt Kuhlmann was asked about the concept of " Dragon Breaks "—time getting all weird on account of magic and stuff⁠—in Elder Scrolls lore.
body: I love this story: Simple serendipity, a workplace oopsie, accidentally setting in motion the continuity and story beats of a billion-dollar franchise. Kirkbride is memetically famous among Elder Scrolls fans as a boundary-pushing loremaster who added a lot of weird flavor to Morrowind, so his affinity for the timey-wimey, fucky-wucky potential of the Dragon Break absolutely scans.

As far as I can tell, it doesn't seem like the series timeline Kuhlmann mentioned was ever publicly available⁠—this must have been an internal lore bible sort of thing. While TES Arena and Daggerfall designer Ted Peterson would write the in-game book, " The Warp in the West," for Oblivion, Kirkbride and Kuhlmann appear to have introduced the concept in Morrowind with the books " Where Were You When the Dragon Broke " and " Dragon Break Re-Examined " respectively.

body: An extremely busy week at the Foundry but the Direct cannot be stopped - the team discuss the latest news as the "Xbox Reset" enters Phase Two and Halo is shipped off to Activision. Meanwhile, Rich, Oliver and Tom join forces to run the rule over Silent Hill Townfall, becauise the show moves on to discuss the implications of the next-gen consoles' respective GPU TFLOPs numbers. And finally, ending the show on a high note, Rich revisits 007 First Light path tracing, finding a night and day improvement in performance over the original release.

videos.title: Kalanoro – Launch Trailer – Nintendo Switch
videos.summary: Play Kalanoro now on Nintendo Switch:
body: Hop on a colorful action-adventure inspired by Malagasy folklore! Recruit legendary lemur musicians, grow your band's fame across Lemuria, and challenge the evil witch Raneny in a quest to save the island—one song at a time!

Once a paradise, the island of Lemuria now suffers under Raneny’s ruthless rule. Having grown tired of exploiting its people, she decided to host a huge concert with the island’s most famous band. You’re sent on a mission to fight back by rallying legendary musicians to your cause!

Dash through diverse biomes, save and befriend funky locals to form your crew, and jump over industrial platforming traps to become Lemuria’s number one band and finally face Raneny. Defeat her minions in fast-paced combat, using hair-based powers and improvised weapons (slippers included). Fight epic and groovy boss battles, and free the island!
